task.title: Add a high-confidence Roleplay prose quality gate
task.source: Reported Roleplay writing issues and AI-like prose patterns
task.classification: engine generation, prompt enforcement, and settings copy

coreClaim: Roleplay generations with strong, locally detectable prose or player-agency problems receive a bounded exact-span correction pass, while clean replies and non-Roleplay modes keep their existing one-call path and unusable corrections preserve the original response.
rootCause: Roleplay prompts requested good prose but the generation boundary did not inspect completed text or safely correct high-confidence violations, so instruction drift could reach the transcript unchanged.

inScope: A bounded exact-span model correction pass
outOfScope: Calling a model on every Roleplay response
Exhaustive player-agency verb detection in every language

claimBoundary.coreClaim: Only strong local evidence or corroborated minor signals route Roleplay text to a constrained editor; accepted edits are exact, non-overlapping, authorized, non-expanding replacements and all invalid editor output falls back to the original.
entrypoints: Roleplay regeneration and continuation through startGeneration
currentPathsOrFormats: JSON exact-span edit arrays with before, after, reason, and description
legacyPathsOrFormats: Clean Roleplay replies retain the existing one-call path
Conversation and Game generation remain outside the Roleplay quality gate
Invalid or unusable editor responses retain the original assistant text
outOfScopeClaims: No claim that subjective writing quality can be fully classified by local code.
No claim that strict player-agency detection is exhaustive outside English.
No new mode, panel, or discoverable workflow is introduced.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: The Roleplay generation owner requested prose constraints but did not enforce high-confidence violations after the model completed a reply.
contractLaneGate.producer: src/engine/generation/start-generation.ts and the selected language-model connection
contractLaneGate.consumer: Roleplay transcript persistence, dry-run previews, and users reading generated scene prose
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: Roleplay text should respect explicit prose and player-agency constraints without adding routine latency or allowing a corrective model call to replace valid output with malformed or broader text.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: src/engine/generation/roleplay-quality-signals.ts performs local routing, roleplay-quality-audit.ts validates bounded exact-span edits, and start-generation.ts applies the same fail-closed correction path to production and dry-run output.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The engine generation orchestrator owns completed model output and mode separation; the settings UI only explains the engine behavior.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not patch one Roleplay or character prompt, run an AI judge on every reply, apply whole-response rewrites, or make React responsible for generation correctness.
regressionProof: Focused signal, audit, agent-runner, and start-generation suites prove routing, exact-span validation, one-call controls, mode separation, and dry-run parity.
The opt-in real-model benchmark exercises eight diverse clean scenes and five injected suspicious replies through production dry-run generation.

positiveRows.claim: Clean and diverse Roleplay responses keep the one-call fast path.
positiveRows.evidence: Deterministic one-call controls pass, and the real-model matrix kept 7 of 8 clean scenarios on one call.

positiveRows.claim: High-confidence repetition, echo, malformed text, identity contradiction, cast saturation, length mismatch, and strict player-agency candidates can route to correction.
positiveRows.evidence: roleplay-quality-signals.spec.ts passes direct and corroborated routing rows while rejecting isolated minor evidence.

positiveRows.claim: Accepted editor output changes only explicitly authorized exact spans and cannot lengthen the response.
positiveRows.evidence: roleplay-quality-audit.spec.ts passes valid multi-edit application, authorization, overlap, ambiguity, no-op, and expansion checks.

positiveRows.claim: Production and dry-run Roleplay generation share the same correction path.
positiveRows.evidence: start-generation focused suites pass saved generation, continuation, and dry-run correction rows.

contradictionRows.claim: Conversation and Game responses must not receive Roleplay correction calls.
contradictionRows.evidence: Focused start-generation mode controls assert one provider call and no quality correction outside Roleplay.

contradictionRows.claim: A single weak or subjective style clue must not add a model call.
contradictionRows.evidence: Signal tests require one high-confidence kind, two independent minor kinds, or at least three corroborating occurrences.

contradictionRows.claim: Malformed, overlapping, unauthorized, ambiguous, expanding, empty, structured, or no-op editor output must not replace the original.
contradictionRows.evidence: Audit validator negative rows pass and the real-model echo/rhetorical retry preserved the original when the editor returned unusable output.

contradictionRows.claim: Player-agency restrictions must not leak into correction prompts for unrelated signal kinds.
contradictionRows.evidence: Prompt contract tests assert agency guidance is conditional on an agency signal.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Legacy visual_novel mode aliases receive the same Roleplay protection.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Mode contract and generation tests include Roleplay and legacy visual_novel routing.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Existing chats without the enabled Roleplay quality setting retain prior behavior.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Agent runner and start-generation tests cover disabled audit and unchanged response paths.

untestedRows: Strict player-agency verb detection is strongest in English; adding equivalent exhaustive rules for every supported language would require separate language-specific work.
No visual screenshot was captured because the UI change is explanatory settings copy rather than layout or interaction behavior.

ownedFacts.description: Local signal detection runs before any optional editor call, so a clean reply does not consume a second model request.
ownedFacts.evidence: Focused agent-runner and start-generation tests assert provider call counts for clean controls.

ownedFacts.description: Invalid corrections preserve the exact original response.
ownedFacts.evidence: Audit validator negative rows and the live echo/rhetorical failure case both retained the original.

ownedFacts.description: The real-model matrix completed eight diverse scenarios without empty output or leaked internal tags.
ownedFacts.evidence: docs/benchmarks/roleplay-quality-live-2026-07-27.md records the isolated production dry-run benchmark.

manualBlockers.reason: The feature is intentionally high-confidence and fail-closed; repetition, echo, length, structure, and malformed-output signals remain language-agnostic while English agency coverage is documented and tested.
The control already existed and only its explanatory copy changed; typecheck, settings information-architecture tests, and the full repository check cover the change.

verification.baselineEvidence: Architecture, security, storage contracts, TypeScript, docs, discovery, workflow protection, Rust workspace compilation, Bunny guidance, and the non-blocking unused-code report completed with exit code 0.
edgeRowsTested: One strong signal versus corroborated minor signals
Roleplay, legacy visual_novel, Conversation, and Game modes
Saved generation, continuation, and dry-run paths
negativeRowsTested: Malformed or unusable editor output preserves the original
Unrelated signals omit player-agency prompt policy
afterEvidence: pnpm exec prettier --check on all changed files
